diagnostics.title: Request-log file append failed (log dropped)
diagnostics.summary: Writing a line to the request-log file failed, so that log line was dropped. Telemetry writes are fire-and-forget and never block serving, but a persistent failure means request logs are being lost — usually a disk-full or permission problem.
diagnostics.action: Check the log file's path for free space and write permission. Serving is unaffected; only request-log durability is.

diagnostics.title: Request-log file open failed (log dropped)
diagnostics.summary: The request-log file could not be opened for append, so that log line was dropped. A persistent failure means request logs are being lost — usually a missing directory, a permission problem, or a full disk.
diagnostics.action: Ensure the log file's directory exists and is writable, and that the disk is not full. Serving is unaffected; only request-log durability is.

diagnostics.title: Request-log archive retention cleanup failed
diagnostics.summary: During rotation, deleting the oldest request-log archive failed, so the archive series may grow past its retention limit and consume more disk than intended. No log data is lost by this failure itself.
diagnostics.action: Check the log directory's permissions and free space so retention cleanup can remove the oldest archive on the next rotation.

diagnostics.title: Request-log archive shift failed during rotation
diagnostics.summary: Renaming an archived request-log file to its next slot during rotation failed, so the older archive was left in place rather than lost. Rotation degrades but no recorded data is discarded.
diagnostics.action: Check the log directory's permissions and that no external process holds the archive files, so the shift can complete on the next rotation.

diagnostics.title: Request-log rotation rename failed (file grows past cap)
diagnostics.summary: Renaming the current request-log file to its first archive slot failed, so busbar keeps APPENDING to the current file rather than truncating it — no recorded data is lost, but the file will grow past its `rotate_mb` cap until this is resolved.
diagnostics.action: Check the log directory's permissions and free space so the rotation rename can succeed. No data is lost in the meantime; the file simply exceeds its size cap.
